newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt blocks utility Jihomoravska div.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt blocks utility Jihomoravska div.

text.p: The Czech National Property Fund (NPF), as expected, on Monday blocked a proposal by the board of power utility Jihomoravska Energeticka a.s. to pay out a 51 crown gross dividend on 1996 earnings, a company offical said.
The firm's Financial Director Jiri Ruzicka told Reuters that shareholders approved the fund's proposal not to pay any dividend at all, after a 40 crown gross dividend in the previous year.
The NPF, the state privatisation agency, holds controlling stakes in all of the Czech Republic's 16 regional power and gas utilities, as well as in the main power generator, CEZ a.s. .
The NPF had said it would vote against dividend payments by all of the utilities because of investment needs for modernisation.
The NPF also said it would be politically unjustifiable for the energey companies to pay dividends at the same time as consumers are facing price hikes.
Power companies use revenues from sales to industrial customers to subsidise lower household prices.
The governmeet has agreed to bring residential rates in line with costs over the next few years.
